newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says Telstra will meet govt promises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says Telstra will meet govt promises.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard, challenged on a proposal to increase telephone charges, said on Wednesday that government-owned telecoms carrier Telstra Corp would do nothing contrary to his pre-election promises.

Earlier on Wednesday, Telstra said it planned to charge 50 cents a call for directory assistance services as part of a A$50 million package of price reductions. Howard promised, prior to the coalition's election win in March last year, that his government would not permit carriers to charge for operator assisted calls, including directory assistance.
"As far as I'm concerned, Telstra won't be doing anything in this area that is contrary to pre-election commitments," Howard told Parliament.
Howard said he could not recall holding any discussions with Telstra chief executive Frank Blount about the carrier's plan and confirmed that he had not forgotten the coalition's promise.
"I've had a number of discussions with Mr Frank Blount, but I do not recall this issue having ever been raised," he said.
Telstra said the plan could allow it to reduce fixed telephone line rentals by A$5 a year and could include enhanced directory services at reduced prices.
It said the plan was still an informal one at this stage and consumer groups would be consulted before a formal proposal was presented to the government.
